Legal

Privacy Policy

This page explains the kinds of information Gabber may process, why it is needed, and the choices available to users.

Launch review required: This policy is an operational draft dated 18 October 2026. Add the final legal entity, registered address and official support email before public release, and have the text reviewed against the production system.

1. Information you provide

Gabber may collect your mobile number for sign-in, profile details such as your name, photo, about text and optional email, the content you choose to send, and business information you submit when registering a business.

2. Contacts and device permissions

If you grant permission, Gabber reads phone numbers from your device contacts so it can identify contacts who use Gabber and help you invite others. Permission can be removed in your device settings. Gabber may also request camera, microphone, photos, location and notification access only when a feature needs it.

3. Communications and activity

Gabber processes messages, media, call signalling, group membership, status updates, delivery information and safety reports to operate the service. Technical information such as device identifiers, IP address, error logs and timestamps may be processed for security, troubleshooting and abuse prevention.

4. Location and business discovery

When you choose to use nearby discovery or auto-detect a business location, Gabber may process approximate or precise location information depending on your device permission. You may deny or revoke location access.

5. Payments and verification

Payment providers and identity or business-verification providers may process information required to complete a transaction or verification. Gabber should not store full card or UPI credentials. The provider's own privacy terms may also apply.

6. How information is used

  • Provide authentication, messaging, calling, status, group and business features.
  • Deliver notifications and requested transactions.
  • Detect abuse, investigate reports and protect users.
  • Maintain, troubleshoot and improve service reliability.
  • Meet applicable legal obligations.

7. Sharing

Information may be shared with other users when you choose to communicate or publish profile, status or business information; with service providers that operate hosting, notifications, storage, payments or verification; or where disclosure is legally required. Gabber does not claim to sell personal information.

8. Retention and deletion

Information is retained for as long as needed to provide the service, maintain security, resolve disputes and meet legal requirements. Some records may remain for a limited period in backups or where retention is legally required. See the account deletion page for the current request process.

9. Security

Gabber uses administrative and technical safeguards intended to protect information. No internet service can guarantee absolute security. Do not describe communications as end-to-end encrypted unless that protection has been independently implemented and verified in the production release.

10. Children

The final launch policy must specify the service's minimum user age and the process used for under-age accounts according to the markets where Gabber is offered.

11. Your choices

You may update profile information, manage device permissions, block users, report content and request account deletion. Additional rights may apply under local law.

12. Contact and updates

An official privacy contact email and registered business address must be added before public launch. Material policy changes should be published here with an updated effective date.
